problems.oneLiner: Remember everything you've passed in a hash set; a duplicate is any value that's already there.
problems.title: Contains Duplicate

problems.oneLiner: Anagrams have identical letter counts - count up for s, down for t, and check everything cancels.
problems.title: Valid Anagram

problems.oneLiner: Don't search for pairs. For each x, ask one O(1) question: have I already seen target − x?
problems.title: Two Sum

problems.oneLiner: Map every word to a key that all its anagrams share (sorted letters or letter counts), then bucket by key.
problems.title: Group Anagrams

problems.oneLiner: Count, then index buckets by frequency (frequencies are bounded by n) and read them from the top down.
problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements

problems.oneLiner: Prefix every string with its length and a delimiter; the decoder jumps over the payload instead of scanning it.
problems.title: Encode and Decode Strings

problems.oneLiner: Everything-except-i = (everything left of i) × (everything right of i). Two sweeps with running products.
problems.title: Product of Array Except Self

problems.oneLiner: Give every row, column and box its own seen-set; cell (r, c) belongs to box (r // 3, c // 3).
problems.title: Valid Sudoku

problems.oneLiner: Put everything in a set; a number starts a run iff num − 1 is missing - only walk forward from those.
problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence

problems.oneLiner: Walk inward from both ends, skipping junk, comparing lowercased characters - no cleaned copy needed.
problems.title: Valid Palindrome

problems.oneLiner: Sum too small → move the left pointer up; too big → move the right pointer down. Sortedness makes each move safe.
problems.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

problems.oneLiner: Sort, fix each anchor, and run Two Sum II on the rest; skip equal neighbours to avoid duplicate triplets.
problems.title: 3Sum

problems.oneLiner: Start wide; the shorter wall limits every narrower container that keeps it, so move the shorter wall inward.
problems.title: Container With Most Water

problems.oneLiner: Water at i = min(maxLeft, maxRight) − h[i]. Move the pointer whose max is smaller: that side's water level is already decided.
problems.title: Trapping Rain Water

problems.oneLiner: Sweep once, remembering the cheapest buy so far; each day's best sale is price − cheapest-so-far.
problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

problems.oneLiner: Grow right; while the new character is a duplicate, shrink left. The window is always repeat-free.
problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

problems.oneLiner: Window is valid iff len − maxFreq ≤ k. Grow right, shrink left while invalid.
problems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement

problems.oneLiner: Slide a window of length len(s1) across s2, updating counts in O(1) per step; a match is equal counts.
problems.title: Permutation in String

problems.oneLiner: Grow r until the window covers t, then advance l as far as it stays valid; record the best each time.
problems.title: Minimum Window Substring

problems.oneLiner: Keep indices whose values strictly decrease; new elements evict smaller ones from the back, expired indices fall off the front, and the front is always the max.
problems.title: Sliding Window Maximum

problems.oneLiner: Push openers; every closer must match the top of the stack; valid iff the stack ends empty.
problems.title: Valid Parentheses

problems.oneLiner: Store, alongside each element, the minimum of everything at or below it; getMin is the top of that record.
problems.title: Min Stack

problems.oneLiner: Push numbers; each operator pops right then left, applies, and pushes the result.
problems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation

problems.oneLiner: Build left to right: '(' if opened < n, ')' if closed < opened. Every completed path is valid.
problems.title: Generate Parentheses

problems.oneLiner: Keep unanswered days on a stack; a warmer day pops and answers every colder day on top.
problems.title: Daily Temperatures

problems.oneLiner: Sort by position from the target backwards; a car merges if its time ≤ the fleet ahead's time, else it starts a new fleet.
problems.title: Car Fleet

problems.oneLiner: Every bar's best rectangle spans until the next shorter bar on each side; an increasing stack finds both edges as bars are popped.
problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram

problems.oneLiner: Save next, flip curr.next to prev, advance - until curr is None; prev is the new head.
problems.title: Reverse Linked List

problems.oneLiner: Start from a dummy node; repeatedly append the smaller head; finally attach the non-empty remainder.
problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists

problems.oneLiner: slow moves 1, fast moves 2; they meet iff there's a cycle, otherwise fast hits None.
problems.title: Linked List Cycle

problems.oneLiner: Find the middle with fast/slow, reverse the second half, then interleave the two halves.
problems.title: Reorder List

problems.oneLiner: Advance `right` n steps, then move both until `right` is None; `left` is just before the target.
problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List

problems.oneLiner: Pass 1 creates a copy of every node in a map; pass 2 sets copy.next = map[old.next] and copy.random = map[old.random].
problems.title: Copy List with Random Pointer

problems.oneLiner: Add digit by digit with a carry, treating a missing digit as 0, and keep going while a carry remains.
problems.title: Add Two Numbers

problems.oneLiner: Follow i → nums[i] from index 0; the duplicate is the entrance of the cycle, found with Floyd's two phases.
problems.title: Find the Duplicate Number

problems.oneLiner: The map finds a node in O(1); the doubly linked list reorders it in O(1); the least recent node sits next to the left sentinel.
problems.title: LRU Cache

problems.oneLiner: Keep the k current heads in a min-heap; repeatedly pop the smallest and push its successor.
problems.title: Merge k Sorted Lists

problems.oneLiner: For each full group: find its kth node, reverse it with prev = the node after the group, then hook group_prev to the new first node.
problems.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
